title: Refactor on-call diagnostics workflow and SLO toolkit helpers
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Refactors on-call diagnostics workflow and SLO toolkit helpers to improve routing, reduce noise, and make runbook linking more reliable. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: on-call workflows were accumulating noisy diagnostics and duplicate runbook links across escalation paths. This made SLO-linked recommendations less useful and increased cognitive load for responders. This change refactors the diagnostics pipeline, consolidates SLO toolkit helper utilities, and adds heuristics to de-duplicate and prioritize runbook suggestions.

Summary of changes: consolidated diagnostics routing into a single workflow handler, introduced an explicit priority scoring step for runbook suggestions (SLO-aware), added batching and debounce logic to avoid duplicate suggestions during incident floods, and extracted common helper functions in slo_toolkit for reuse by incident-bot and the SLO service. The refactor intentionally keeps public CLI/HTTP endpoints stable; most changes are internal restructuring and behaviour improvements.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate diagnostics routing into incident-bot/diagnostics/workflow.py
- [x] Add priority scoring heuristic (SLO weight + confidence)
- [x] Extract slo_toolkit/helpers.py with test coverage
- [x] Add debounce/batching guard to runbook suggestion emitter
- [x] Update runbook linking to prefer high-confidence SLO matches
- [x] Add end-to-end smoke test for on-call flow
- [x] Update documentation comments and Linear references

Testing notes: unit tests added for priority scoring and helpers (coverage +6%). Integration smoke test simulates an SLO breach and verifies that only top-3 runbook suggestions are emitted and that duplicate suggestions within a 30s window are suppressed. Manual staging validation performed against a synthetic incident stream.

Linear/Jira: ENG-2147 (on-call diagnostics refactor), ENG-2210 (slo-toolkit helpers consolidation), SUP-622 (customer incident that motivated duplicate suggestions).

Backward compatibility: No breaking public API changes. The emitted event schema for internal runbook suggestions gains an optional "priority_score" numeric field; consumers that ignore unknown fields will be unaffected.

Rollout plan: feature-gated behind incident-bot.experimental.diagnostics_v2; staged rollout to 10% of orgs for 48 hours, then 50%, monitor runbook suggestion volume and false-positive rate.
